fatal_errors: The central refined-grain and grain-boundary-mediated mechanism is asserted without evidence that the as-cast WTaTiVZr alloy has refined grains or that grain boundaries control its toughness.
Matching the alloy and tungsten grain-size distributions removes the proposed grain-refinement contrast, so the experiment cannot isolate grain refinement as the cause.
The proposed 1000–1200 °C tensile and creep tests do not reconstruct the reported quasi-static compression, room-temperature scratch, and indentation measurements from room temperature to 500 °C.
The cited evidence concerns other HEAs or general tungsten behavior and does not directly establish grain-boundary dislocation nucleation as the mechanism in WTaTiVZr.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the requested comparison and correctly predicts greater plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten, but it misses the material-specific mechanism and evidence. The reported alloy is a solidification-segregated, dual-BCC material with W-Ta-rich dendrites and Ti-Zr-rich interdendritic regions; its strength was interpreted through multicomponent solid-solution strengthening, lattice distortion, and frictional resistance, while improved damage tolerance was associated more cautiously with Ti, V, and Zr effects on dislocations, cohesion, localized plasticity, and crack propagation. Grain refinement and dominant grain-boundary nucleation were not demonstrated. The proposed tests at 1000–1200 °C also lie far outside the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C evidence window, where the key observations were approximately 6% room-temperature plastic strain, crack disappearance above 200 °C, strength retention to 500 °C, and scratch toughness of about 38 versus 25 MPa√m. Although E4 and E6–E7 provide generic support for interface-mediated deformation and E9 discusses high-temperature grain-boundary or recrystallization behavior in another RHEA, none validates the claimed mechanism in this alloy. The falsification rule tests overall performance and correlated boundary activity, but not whether grain-boundary nucleation rather than chemistry, phase segregation, lattice distortion, or crack-path effects causes the advantage.
